{{ElectionsOH}}
The '''2014 Ohio gubernatorial election''' took place on November 4, 2014. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Governor [[John Kasich]] won a second term by a landslide over [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] candidate [[Ed FitzGerald]] and [[Green Party (United States)|Green Party]] candidate [[Anita Rios]]. [[Partisan primary|Primary elections]] were held on May 6, 2014.

Kasich's [[landslide victory]] gave him the highest percentage of the vote since [[George Voinovich]]'s win in [[1994 Ohio gubernatorial election|1994]], a large improvement from his narrow victory in [[2010 Ohio gubernatorial election|2010]]. {{As of|2024}}, this was the last time the counties of [[Cuyahoga County, Ohio|Cuyahoga]] and [[Franklin County, Ohio|Franklin]] voted for the Republican candidate and the last time [[Monroe County, Ohio|Monroe County]] voted for the Democratic candidate.

This was one of the nine Republican-held governorships up for election in a state that [[Barack Obama]] won in the [[2012 United States presidential election|2012 presidential election]].

==Background==
Kasich, who was elected with [[Tea Party movement|Tea Party]] support [[2010 Ohio gubernatorial election|in 2010]], faced considerable backlash from the movement. His decision to accept the [[Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act]]'s expansion of [[Medicaid]], his increased spending, taxation of [[Hydraulic fracturing|fracking]] on Ohio farmland and perceived failure to go far enough on charter schools and school vouchers caused Tea Party groups to refuse to support his campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/03/11/john-kasich-tea-party_n_2854815.html|title=John Kasich Faces Tea Party Protest Over Medicaid Decision|date=March 11, 2013|access-date=September 5, 2013|work=HuffPost|first=Amanda|last=Terkel}}</ref> When Kasich passed over Tea Party leader Tom Zawistowski for the position of executive director of the [[Ohio Republican Party]] in favor of [[Matt Borges]], who worked with a gay rights group, that was widely seen as the last straw.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2013/05/06/why-does-the-tea-party-want-to-let-democrats-run-ohio.html|title=Why Does the Tea Party Want to Let Democrats Run Ohio?|date=May 6, 2013|access-date=September 5, 2013|work=The Daily Beast|first=Justin|last=Green}}</ref> Tea Party groups announced they would support a primary challenger, or, if none emerged, the [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]] nominee. Zawistowski said, "John Kasich is going to lose in 2014. We don't care who else wins."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thedailybeast.com/articles/2013/09/04/ohio-republican-party-goes-to-war-with-itself-leaving-2016-in-doubt.html|title=Ohio Republican Party Goes to War With Itself, Leaving 2016 in Doubt|date=September 4, 2013|access-date=September 5, 2013|work=The Daily Beast|first=David|last=Freedlander}}</ref> Ultimately, Kasich was unopposed in the Republican primary.

==Libertarian primary==
[[Charlie Earl]] gathered enough raw signatures to obtain ballot access.<ref name="qualify1">{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/open/index.ssf/2014/02/ed_fitzgerald_faces_only_prima.html|title=Ed FitzGerald faces only primary among statewide candidates; Libertarians fail to field full slate|last=Gomez|first=Henry J.|work=[[The Plain Dealer]]|date=February 18, 2014|access-date=March 3, 2014}}</ref> However, he was removed from the ballot because technical faults in collection rendered many of his signatures invalid. The decision was appealed in federal court.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dispatch.com/content/stories/local/2014/03/09/libertarians-angry-at-gop-while-acknowledging-faults.html|title=Libertarians angry at GOP while acknowledging faults|author=Joe Vardon|work=The Columbus Dispatch|access-date=November 26, 2014}}</ref>

==General election==

===Campaign===
FitzGerald released a plan for state-funded universal preschool in addition to announcing his support for gay marriage.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/open/index.ssf/2014/05/fitzgerald_proposes_500_millio.html#incart_river_default|title=FitzGerald proposes $500&nbsp;million universal preschool plan|work=The Plain Dealer|date=May 14, 2014|access-date=November 26, 2014}}</ref> He criticized Kasich for signing into law income tax cuts that save larger sums of money for wealthier Ohioans than poorer ones, while increasing sales taxes, which tax a larger percentage of income from poorer Ohioans than from wealthier ones.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/open/index.ssf/2013/06/ed_fitzgerald_assails_ohio_bud.html#incart_river_default|title=Ed FitzGerald assails Ohio budget as harmful to middle-class families, the poor and women|work=The Plain Dealer|date=June 28, 2013|access-date=November 26, 2014}}</ref> FitzGerald also chided Kasich for a lack of transparency at JobsOhio, the privatized economic development agency that Kasich formed,<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20140517124037/https://www.nbc4i.com/story/25393739/jobs-ohio-doesnt-have-to-disclose-records-on-taxpayer-money Jobs Ohio Doesn't Have To Disclose Records On Taxpayer Money]</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://wosu.org/2012/news/2013/09/09/ed-fitzgerald-calls-for-jobsohio-transparency/|title=Ed FitzGerald Calls For JobsOhio Transparency|work=WOSU News|access-date=November 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517122919/http://wosu.org/2012/news/2013/09/09/ed-fitzgerald-calls-for-jobsohio-transparency/|archive-date=May 17, 2014|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/politics/elections/2014/03/21/ed-fitzgerald-enquirer-ohio/6713217/|title=Ed FitzGerald to Enquirer: Here's my Ohio|work=The Cincinnati Enquirer|date=March 21, 2014|access-date=November 26, 2014}}</ref> and for signing into law bills that cut early voting days and limit the distribution of absentee ballot applications.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/open/index.ssf/2014/02/kasich_signs_voting_bills_that.html|title=Kasich signs voting bills that end Golden Week and limit distribution of absentee ballots|work=The Plain Dealer|date=February 22, 2014|access-date=November 26, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cuyahoga-county/index.ssf/2014/04/cuyahoga_county_council_gives_final_approval_to_ed_fitzgeralds_voting_rights_law.html|title=Cuyahoga County|work=The Plain Dealer|date=April 9, 2014|access-date=November 26, 2014}}</ref> FitzGerald faced several scandals that damaged his candidacy, most notably the revelations that he had driven for several years without a valid driver's license, him being found in a car late at night with a woman who was not his wife, and that his initial running mate, State Sen. Eric Kearney, owed over $1 million in unpaid taxes. Additionally, FitzGerald consistently trailed Kasich in fundraising throughout the entire campaign.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cleveland.com/opinion/2014/08/ed_fitzgeralds_campaign_is_ove.html|title=Ed FitzGerald's campaign is over except for the epitaph, but he may take down the rest of the ticket, too: Brent Larkin|date=August 6, 2014|work=The Plain Dealer}}</ref>
